questions.q: Identify the grammatical category of the word "lehj&lkxj" in the line "frjrh gS lehj&lkxj ij" and name the specific समास (compound) type it represents.
questions.a: "lehj&lkxj" is a संयुक्त पद (compound word) representing the तत्पुरुष समास (specifically, द्वितीया तत्पुरुष) where "lehj" (body) is the object/location and "lkxj" (heat) modifies it — "heat on the body". A wrong answer like "कर्मधारय समास" reveals the student cannot distinguish between appositional (कर्मधारय) and case-governed (तत्पुरुष) compounds, a critical error for board exams where समास identification carries 2-3 marks.

questions.q: Explain why the poet uses the Braj Bhasha verb form "gSa" (in "g¡lrs gSa NksVs ikSèks y?kqHkkj") instead of the standard Khari Boli "hEṅ" — what grammatical and affective function does this serve?
questions.a: "gSa" is the Braj Bhasha plural present indicative form (equivalent to Khari Boli "hEṅ"), used here to maintain the poem's metrical rhythm (मात्रिक छंद) and regional authenticity. It creates a folk-song cadence that mirrors the children's spontaneous joy. A student who says "it's just old Hindi" misses the deliberate metrical and sociolinguistic choice — a common error where students confuse dialectal grammar with "incorrect" grammar, losing marks in "language usage" questions.

questions.q: In the line "v'kfu&ikr ls 'kkfir mÂr 'kr&'kr ohj", identify the postpositions and case endings used. Then rewrite the phrase in standard Khari Boli prose order (अन्वय) and explain the grammatical shift.
questions.a: Postpositions: "ls" (ablative/instrumental), "mÂr" (locative, Braj form of "mẽ"). Case: "v'kfu&ikr" (otzikr) is in कारक (case) governed by "ls". अन्वय: "otzikr se sakal mẽ phir-phir ohj (aata hai)". The shift: Braj uses "mÂr" for locative where Khari Boli uses "mẽ"; poetic inversion places "ohj" at end for rhyme with "vpy&'kjhj". A student who only translates without showing case-postposition mapping fails to demonstrate grammatical analysis — a JEE/NEET humanities trap where surface meaning is mistaken for structural understanding.

questions.q: Compare the syntactic structure of the two refrain-like lines: "ckny jkx" (repeated 5 times) and ",s foIyo osQ ohj!" (repeated 3 times). How does the grammatical minimalism (absence of verbs, copulas) in these lines function differently from the full sentences in the stanzas?
questions.a: "ckny jkx" is a nominal phrase (noun + noun in apposition or vocative) acting as a thematic anchor — no verb, timeless. ",s foIyo osQ ohj!" is a noun phrase with possessive postposition "osQ" + noun "ohj", functioning as an exclamatory apostrophe to summer. The full sentences (e.g., "frjrh gS lehj&lkxj ij") use copula "gS" to assert states. The refrain lines suspend predication, turning grammar into incantation. A student who calls both "titles" or "headings" misses the syntactic distinction between a bare NP and a possessive NP — a subtle but board-relevant grammatical nuance.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "The poem's use of Braj Bhasha grammar is merely decorative; the same meaning could be conveyed in standard Khari Boli without loss." Defend or refute using three specific grammatical evidence points from the text.
questions.a: Refute. (1) Metrical necessity: "gSa" (2 syllables) vs "hEṅ" (2 but different weight) — the मात्रिक छंद requires specific laghu/guru patterns only Braj forms satisfy. (2) Semantic density: "v^kfydk" (compound: वक् + फटिक? — actually वक् + फटिक? No, वक् + फटिक is not standard; likely वक् + फटिक = वक्फटिक? Wait — from word meaning: "v^kfydk  ugha gS js" — "v^kfydk" = "वक् + फटिक"? Actually word meaning says: "v^kfydk  ugha gS js" — no gloss. But "v^kfydk" is likely a Braj compound meaning "fickle" or "momentary". Its internal sandhi/consonant cluster is phonologically Braj. (3) Sociolinguistic indexing: "v'kfu&ikr" (otzikr) for "evening" marks rural registers. Khari Boli "shaam" loses the cultural texture. A student who agrees reveals a fundamental misconception: that grammar is a neutral container for meaning, not a meaning-making system.

questions.q: Create two new lines in the style of "ckny jkx" that use: (a) a तत्पुरुष समास with a body-part noun, (b) a Braj-style verb ending in "gS" or "gSa", and (c) an inverted word order for rhyme. Gloss your grammatical choices.
questions.a:
Example:  
"nq[k dk dV;k gS nXèk ij"  
"fiQj fiQj vk;k gSa ckny dk th"  
Gloss: (a) "nq[k dk dV;k" — तत्पुरुष (षष्ठी) — "pain of the nose" (body part). (b) "gS", "gSa" — Braj present indicative. (c) Inversion: "nXèk ij nq[k dk dV;k gS" → "nq[k dk dV;k gS nXèk ij" for rhyme with "th". A poor answer uses Khari Boli verbs ("hai", "hain"), no compound, or normal SVO order — showing inability to internalize the grammatical system as a creative tool.
